shorts.title: What Was the Edward Jenner Experiment?
shorts.description:
Why Vaccines Are Named After a Cow
https://www.youtube.com/@HistoryOfScienceYT

On 1 July 1796, Edward Jenner tested whether cowpox had protected James from smallpox. No disease followed.

shorts.title: Why Is It Called a Vaccine?
shorts.description:
Why Vaccines Are Named After a Cow
https://www.youtube.com/@HistoryOfScienceYT

Twenty-two years before Edward Jenner's 1798 book, Benjamin Jesty tried cowpox in 1774. Jenner called the disease variolae vaccinae ("smallpox of the cow"), and from vacca, the Latin word for cow, came the name vaccination.
